about: Voiceover for the second demo cut (start page, five puzzles). One audio file per line; lines split where a Higgsfield clip cuts in (s03b, s07a, s08a) and around the IonQ wait (s09a / s09b). 'text' is the caption, 'tts' (when present) is what the voice reads. The finished track (2:55.6) and the timed captions (captions_v2.srt) are built with vo_clean.py, assemble.py and make_captions.py; see docs/VIDEO_SCRIPT.md for the cue sheet the screen recordings follow.

segments.title: Hook
segments.text: Phase Shift is a puzzle game about interference: what makes a quantum computer more than a coin flip.

segments.title: Runs on Qollab
segments.text: It runs on Qollab: press Run, choose IonQ's simulator, and Qiskit starts in your browser.

segments.title: The only rule
segments.text: Here's the only rule you need.

segments.title: Arrows add head to tail
segments.text: Every path carries an arrow. Where paths meet, the arrows add head to tail.

segments.title: Lined up or opposite
segments.text: Lined up, a detector lights up. Opposite, they cancel: it goes dark.

segments.title: Level 1: the phase is invisible
segments.text: Level 1, Invisible Ink. A Hadamard splits the qubit into two paths; a phase turns the lower path's arrow. I run it at 0°: 50/50. I turn it to 180° and run again: still 50/50. The phase is invisible: measuring sees an arrow's length, not its direction.
segments.tts: Level one, Invisible Ink. A Hadamard splits the qubit into two paths; a phase turns the lower path's arrow. I run it at zero degrees: fifty-fifty. I turn it to one-eighty and run again: still fifty-fifty. The phase is invisible: measuring sees an arrow's length, not its direction.

segments.title: Recombine: interference
segments.text: I switch on a second Hadamard so the paths meet. Same phase, run: 100%. Why? Follow the arrows. Classical rules give 50%; quantum rules give 100%. That difference is interference, and no coin flip can reach it.
segments.tts: I switch on a second Hadamard so the paths meet. Same phase, run: one hundred percent. Why? Follow the arrows. Classical rules give fifty percent; quantum rules give one hundred. That difference is interference, and no coin flip can reach it.

segments.title: Levels 2 and 3
segments.text: Dark Port hides a phase: brightness tells you how far you are from dark. In the Eraser, a spying detector kills the interference. Erase what it knows, and interference returns, but only in the correlations.

segments.title: Kickback demo
segments.text: A controlled phase acts only when both qubits are 1. With the target at 0, the phase vanishes. Flip the target with an X, and the phase kicks back onto the control: it reads 1, while the target stays 1. That's the trick behind phase estimation and Shor's algorithm.
segments.tts: A controlled phase acts only when both qubits are one. With the target at zero, the phase vanishes. Flip the target with an X, and the phase kicks back onto the control: it reads one, while the target stays one. That's the trick behind phase estimation and Shor's algorithm.

segments.title: New: Amplifier
segments.text: Also new: level 5, Amplifier, a 2-qubit Grover search.
segments.tts: Also new: level five, Amplifier, a two-qubit Grover search.

segments.title: Amplifier demo
segments.text: The prize is behind door 11. I mark it with a phase. On its own, the mark is invisible: 25% each. The diffuser reflects every arrow about the average. One query: 100%. Four arrows line up on the prize.
segments.tts: The prize is behind door one-one. I mark it with a phase. On its own, the mark is invisible: twenty-five percent each. The diffuser reflects every arrow about the average. One query: one hundred percent. Four arrows line up on the prize.

segments.title: Confirm on IonQ
segments.text: Now, Confirm on IonQ. This exact circuit goes to IonQ's simulator as one job.

segments.title: One job per Run
segments.text: Qollab allows one IonQ job per Run, so you practise in the browser, then confirm once. IonQ agrees: three stars.

segments.title: Phone and accessibility
segments.text: On a phone, Run stays under your thumb. It's keyboard and screen-reader accessible: the histogram is a table, and every arrow is described in text.

segments.title: Open source, tested, extensible
segments.text: It's real Qiskit, MIT licensed, with 207 tests, and every level is checked for IonQ. To add a puzzle, write one Level in levels.py and one feedback function. The interface builds itself.
segments.tts: It's real Qiskit, MIT licensed, with two hundred and seven tests, and every level is checked for IonQ. To add a puzzle, write one Level in levels dot py and one feedback function. The interface builds itself.

segments.title: Outro
segments.text: Phase Shift. Five puzzles, one rule: follow the arrows. Play it on Qollab.
